title: What If You Raised a Chimp With Your Baby? In 1931 a Scientist Did

scenes.text: What if you raised a chimp alongside your baby? In 1931 a psychologist did. It backfired.
Winthrop Kellogg brought home Gua, a seven-month-old chimpanzee, to grow up beside his ten-month-old son.
Both were fed, diapered and tested the same way, twelve hours a day, seven days a week.
At first the chimp was ahead on most tests. She followed commands and fed herself with a spoon.
But she never picked up human speech. And after nine months, something else showed up.
The boy had started copying her, barking for his food like a chimp. The experiment ended, and Gua went back to the primate colony.

description:
What if you raised a chimpanzee as your baby's sibling? In June 1931 the psychologist Winthrop Kellogg took Gua, a chimp about seven months old, into his home to be raised exactly like his ten-month-old son, to see how human an ape could become.
For nine months the two were cared for and tested side by side. Gua did better on most early tasks and learned to obey spoken commands, but never spoke; the boy, meanwhile, began imitating her food barks. The experiment ended in March 1932 and Gua was returned to the primate colony. Kellogg wrote it up as The Ape and the Child.
